newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent looks firmer, NYMEX rebounds.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent looks firmer, NYMEX rebounds.

text.p: Brent crude futures were quoted slightly firmer on Monday from London on Friday, supported by a rebound in NYMEX crudes on ACCESS.
Brokers said they expected prices to find some support from short covering which could prompt a test of $18.00 on May, but the upside would be limited by a physical market overhang.
May was quoted on SIMEX in late afternoon dealings at $17.86/$17.89 per barrel, up from the London settlement of $17.68.

A chart gap between $18.40 and $18.50 was likely to limit the upside potential of the market, brokers said. In addition, until some of the physical overhang starts to disappear, players would be reluctant buyers of fresh long positions.
One broker said he expected Brent to range in the next few weeks between $17.00 and $18.50 with a bear target medium term of $16.80.
May NYMEX crude on ACCESS last traded at $19.25, up 13 cents from New York's close on Friday of $19.12, and one cent under the intraday high.
